agent: running game, the fall-back from a losing defence, 2026-11-10
question: what pulls defenders out of a battle, and in what order
slots_noted: Both functions are already in the record; this fragment adds to their comments.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_FallBackFromLosingDefences
addresses.comment:
**Pulls defenders out of a losing battle.** 0x4D7F80 to the `ret 4` at 0x4D858B; always answers false. Only with the frontier at war and a unit. For each ops-area province p that is not its own depot and has a fort level below 3: for each land battle there (slot 11 == 1) at least 12 hours old (25 at plan stance 3 or more, CCombat +0x1C) in which we are a defending country (defender +0x54) and the attacker's share (slot 17) is above 0.7: p's neighbours (edge kind not 3, land, simulated) are scored - a hostile one across a river (kind 1 or 2) ends the look at this battle; one we may operate in scores effective infrastructure/1000 + 2 x fort level, +10 across a river, +100 if it is p's depot, and /100 if it is in the ops area; if no friendly land unit is already heading into p from a neighbour, the defenders without a blocking order are sent one each, best first, round the list again while defenders remain - stopping at the first ops-area candidate where any candidate lies outside the ops area - with a plain MoveUnit(unit, q, 0, 0, 0, 0), and full_pass_pending (+0x84) set. The name is ours.

**Read again on the listing, 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 24). A river is an edge of kind 1 **or** 2, and only across one is the neighbour's controller asked CCountry::IsEnemy (war or REB), which ends the look at the battle. For every land, simulated neighbour, each unit standing in it that is a land unit, whose owner the country may operate in (CCountry::CanOperateIn) and whose destination (0x89AF00) is the province is counted, and any such unit keeps the defenders in - it is a unit beside the province, not one anywhere. A neighbour is scored only where CanOperateIn answers for its controller. The defenders are the side's land units without UnitHasBlockingOrder, **whoever owns them**, gathered front to back into a list and sent from its back: the last of the side first, one to each scored neighbour in turn.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled from the running game, and its moves logged with their return address: Soviet 129, 112 and 108 out of 2390 to 2333, 2509 and 2449 at the second hour after a load.

addresses.name: CAIUnit_PlaceReserves
addresses.comment:
**Held-back divisions to the rear.** 0x4CB840 to the `ret 4` at 0x4CBFE6. Builds a 0x1C record for each province of the second ring +0xA0 (friendly land two steps out) with cap = round(10 x effective infrastructure) (modifier 12 x (1000 + modifiers 13 and 14) / 1000, held between 10 and 1000), counts the held-back divisions into them, then for each held-back division (+0x15C) not retreating (+0x158), not holding ground (CUnit::IsHoldingGround - in a battle whose other side has somebody), with no blocking order (order slot 24 false) and not a garrison (+0x2C9), each refusal the per-unit continue at VA 0x8CBEE5: unless it stands or heads in a ring province within its cap, it is looked at - beside a war candidate's province (IsWarCandidate) across a river or in a fort and fit (strength and organisation above 0.3) it stays; beside war-candidate land units and fit it stays unless our other idle divisions there number at least half of those units; otherwise it goes to the ring province, other than where it is bound, least by map distance + 20 x have - 30 x (its province's depot hops - that province's), with MoveUnit(0, 1, 1). Answers whether it moved one. The name is ours.

**Read again 2026-11-10** (`FINDINGS-liveread.md`, section 23). The ring's records are filled by CAIUnit::CountUnitsAtPositions over the held-back divisions, any land unit, no allies - so a division standing in one ring province and bound for another is counted in neither. The busy test is the order's slot 24 alone, so a division on its way is looked at. The idle divisions in the outnumbered test are those without UnitHasBlockingOrder. On the save of July 1941 this is what moves Italy's Libyan reserve between 9422 and 5626 every three hours.

The idle divisions counted in the outnumbered test are those of any country the agent's may operate in (CCountry::CanOperateIn at 0x8CBD92), divisions without UnitHasBlockingOrder, not only its own.
